newsitem.title: USA: IBM to make, market Cyrix chip.
newsitem.headline: IBM to make, market Cyrix chip.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp said Friday it will manufacture Cyrix Corp's new Pentium-compatible chip and will market an IBM-branded version.

IBM said its IBM 6x86MX is fully compatible with the newest series of Pentium chips and comes in three versions: the PR166, PR200 and PR233. All three incorporate MMX technology -- multimedia instructions added to the chip architecture.

Earlier today Cyrix introduced its latest challenge to Intel Corp's domination of the personal computer chip industry with a microprocessor that it said competes with the Pentium II at half the price.
IBM said its PR233 outperforms the Pentium II at 233 MHz and costs about $150 less. In quantities of 1,000, the PR233 sells for $477 per chip.
The 6x86MX chip is available now "in limited quantities," IBM said. General availability of the PR166 and PR200 will come in August, and of the PR233 in September, it said.
